label: inferable
contract: A column is as wide as the longer of its header and its widest cell, so a long header keeps the columns aligned.
visible_check:
from tables import render_table
got = render_table(["product", "n"], [["tea", "4"], ["jam", "9"]])
want = "product | n\n--------+--\ntea     | 4\njam     | 9"
assert got == want, got
heldout_check:
from tables import render_table
got = render_table(["name", "id"], [["al", "x1"], ["bo", "y2"]])
assert got == "name | id\n-----+---\nal   | x1\nbo   | y2"

label: inferable
contract: With no rows, the table is just the header line and the separator line.
visible_check:
from tables import render_table
got = render_table(["name"], [])
assert got == "name\n----", repr(got)
heldout_check:
from tables import render_table
assert render_table(["x", "yy"], []) == "x | yy\n--+---"

label: arbitrary
contract: Cells holding int or float values are right-aligned in their column; all other cells are left-aligned.
visible_check:
from tables import render_table
got = render_table(["num", "tag"], [[3, "abc"], [1200, "xyz"]])
want = "num  | tag\n-----+----\n   3 | abc\n1200 | xyz"
assert got == want, got
heldout_check:
from tables import render_table
got = render_table(["qty", "price", "item"], [[5, 2.5, "pear"], [120, 10.25, "plum"]])
assert got == "qty | price | item\n----+-------+-----\n  5 |   2.5 | pear\n120 | 10.25 | plum"

label: arbitrary
contract: A None cell is rendered as an empty cell.
visible_check:
from tables import render_table
got = render_table(["key", "v"], [["k01", "a"], [None, "b"]])
want = "key | v\n----+--\nk01 | a\n    | b"
assert got == want, got
heldout_check:
from tables import render_table
got = render_table(["a", "b"], [[None, "x"], ["yy", "z"]])
assert got == "a  | b\n---+--\n   | x\nyy | z"
